reponse: The root cause was the Kafka broker ingest-kafka-2, not the ingest-worker code: disks hit 100% and the broker went read-only at 09:38 UTC after the retention change in infra PR #221, which removed size-based retention and kept only 7-day time-based retention [2][3]. The broker's read-only state stalled the consumers, producing KafkaConsumerTimeout errors on group ingest-events from 09:39 to 12:24 UTC [4]. The outage lasted 2h47m (09:38–12:25 UTC), with events delayed up to that amount and none lost since producers buffered [2]. The batch-size change in PR #388 was initially suspected but turned out to be a red herring; the revert changed nothing and the change was re-applied on Friday [1][3][5]. Follow-up actions include a disk alert at 80%, restoring size-based retention, and a status page template for ingestion delays [5].
